bullets.text: Protocol: 2–4 x 60 mL thick barium paste via large-bore soft (Miller) catheter; optional small-bowel opacification (500 mL oral barium 30–60 min before); optional vaginal opacification 5 mL; post-evacuation straining image for retained material or enterocele

bullets.text: Sequence: spot lateral at rest in left lateral decubitus, then seated on defecography chair (right lateral view), optional Kegel (lift) and straining images, cine during evacuation, post-evacuation straining image

bullets.text: Evacuation proctography (defecography) is a fluoroscopic (or MR) technique to evaluate pelvic floor prolapse; indications are incomplete or obstructed defecation/constipation, pelvic floor disorder, rectal prolapse and faecal incontinence; a postoperative rectum (e.g. coloanal anastomosis) is a contraindication or needs caution before loading and stressing it.
bullets.label: cited

bullets.text: Defecography technique: a special commode on the fluoroscopy table; barium may be mixed with breadcrumbs, cornflour or porridge powder to give a stool-like consistency; rectal filling stops when the patient has an urge to defecate; optional cine/spot images are taken while straining without defecating; the patient needs privacy.
bullets.label: cited

bullets.text: The anorectal angle is formed by a line parallel to the anal canal and a line parallel to the posterior rectum; its change reflects puborectalis strength; the pelvic floor normally descends a few centimetres on straining, and during normal evacuation the puborectalis impression on the distal posterior rectal wall is lost.
bullets.label: cited

bullets.text: Anorectal angle ~90–95 deg at rest, ~135 deg at evacuation (more obtuse); anorectal junction descent <3.5 cm, usually to ischial tuberosities
bullets.label: cited

bullets.text: Defecography (evacuation proctography): the rectum is opacified with thick barium paste via a catheter, the vagina (and small bowel, for enterocele) may be opacified, and evacuation is imaged in lateral projection with the patient seated on a commode.

bullets.text: Defecography volumes in the paper: 135 mL liquid barium 2 hours before, barium paste ~250 mL, 30 mL of 50% amidotrizoic acid gel in the vagina, video recording (no source found)

bullets.text: Dynamic rectal examination (DRE, defecography) records expulsion of a barium paste that approximates faeces; indications are outlet obstruction (intussusception, enterocele, spastic pelvic floor), distinguishing anterior rectocele from enterocele, and faecal incontinence with intra-anal intussusception; the seated patient is imaged laterally at rest, during squeeze and during evacuation.
